agent.replyHint: A reply is visible to the customer. An internal note is not.
agent.title: Request
automation.actionsHint: Applied in order. Priority only goes up, and an assignee is only filled in when nobody has it — a rule should not overwrite what a person did.
automation.conditionCount: {count, plural, =0 {no conditions — every one} one {# condition} other {# conditions}}
automation.conditionsHint: Conditions are joined with AND. If you need “or”, split it into two rules — that also reads better in the list.
automation.description: Rules change tickets and write to customers while nobody is watching. A change a rule made never wakes automation again.
automation.name: Name
automation.title: Automation
automation.triggerHint: Only tickets where this happened are looked at. A rule runs inside its project only.
canned.description: Shared with everyone on this project. Inserting one gives you a draft to edit, not a message to send.
canned.name: Name
canned.shortcutHint: Optional. Type / followed by this in the comment box.
canned.title: Canned responses
csat.commentHint: What went well, what didn't — it goes straight to the person who handled it.
csat.gone: This survey link no longer works. It has expired, or the address is wrong.
csat.mailBody: We closed your request “{summary}”. A one-tap rating tells us how it went, and helps us handle the next one better.
csat.question: How did we do?
csat.thanks: Thank you — we got your answer.
csat.title: Rate this request
customers.description: Group customers by school or institution. Everyone in an organization sees the organization's requests.
customers.domainsHint: Used to pick a default organization when a customer signs up. It does not decide who sees what — membership does.
customers.membersEmpty: Nobody has joined this organization yet.
customers.name: Name
customers.oneOrgOnly: A customer belongs to one organization. Adding them here moves them out of any other.
customers.title: Customer organizations
email.title: Email channels
email.description: Mail sent to this address becomes a ticket. A public reply continues the same thread in the customer’s inbox.
email.outboundFromHint: Replies go out from here. It may differ from the receiving address, but then customer replies land there.
email.passwordHint: Encrypted on save. It is never shown again.
email.passwordKeptHint: Leave blank to keep the password already stored.
email.useSslHint: Turning this off sends the password in the clear. Only for a dev stack or an internal network.
form.articlesHint: If the answer is already here, you do not have to wait. Send the request anyway if it does not help.
form.guestEmailHint: We send the request number here. Nothing else.
portal.conversationEmpty: No messages yet. We will reply here.
portal.myRequestsEmpty: You have not made any requests yet.
portal.pick: What do you need help with?
portal.pickEmpty: This portal has no request forms yet.
portal.signedOut: You are not signed in. You can still make a request.
portal.title: Support
portal.useThePortal: This account uses the customer portal, not the internal app.
portals.description: A portal is one place customers come to. It belongs to a project.
portals.empty: This project has no portals yet.
portals.isPublicHint: Guests can send a request. Nobody ever sees another customer's requests.
portals.name: Name
portals.noDelete: A portal is closed, never deleted — deleting it would take its forms with it, and tickets would lose which form they came from.
portals.projectMore: More projects match than shown. Type to narrow it down.
portals.slugHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Customers read this in the URL, and it cannot be changed later.
portals.title: Portals
queues.conditionFailed: This queue's condition did not run:
queues.conditionHint: Same query language as issue search. Only tickets appear here, whatever the condition matches.
queues.description: A queue is a live list: it holds a condition, not tickets. Change a ticket and the queues follow.
queues.name: Name
queues.noTickets: Nothing in this queue right now.
queues.title: Queues
queues.truncated: Showing the first 50. Narrow the condition to see the rest.
requestTypes.description: Each form becomes one issue type. Answers land in the ticket.
requestTypes.empty: This portal has no forms yet.
requestTypes.fieldMappingHint: Which custom field holds the answer. Summary and details go into the ticket itself.
requestTypes.issueTypeFixed: The issue type is set when the form is created. Changing it would make every field mapping meaningless.
requestTypes.kbSpaceHint: Suggests published pages from this space while the customer types a title. Only knowledge base spaces can be chosen.
requestTypes.name: Name
requestTypes.title: Request forms
sla.calendarsDescription: Shared across the installation. The calendar owns the timezone — an SLA is one promise, so it needs one clock.
sla.escalationsHint: What to do once a share of the target is used. 100% is the target itself; above that is after the miss.
sla.goalsHint: One line per target, first match wins. Last line must have no condition. For example: priority>=5 1h then 4h
sla.metricImmutable: What a policy measures cannot be changed — already-running clocks would start measuring something else. Make a new policy instead.
sla.name: Name
sla.noCalendars: No business calendars yet. A policy needs one.
sla.noStates: This project has no statuses to choose from — it needs an issue type first.
sla.pauseStatesHint: The clock stops while the ticket sits in one of these — use it for waiting on the customer.
sla.policiesDescription: A policy measures one thing: first response or resolution. Targets are checked against a business calendar, so nights and weekends do not count.
sla.title: SLA
sla.workingHoursHint: One line per weekday: Mon=0. For example 0 09:00-12:00 13:00-18:00
